=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Seller's update note and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA or the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012). Treat the points below as issues to verify against those documents.

---

## 0. The framing in the cover note

The preamble says the positions are "standard", "settled at principal level", "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened." That is the Seller's advocacy, not an agreed position.

- **Confirm with Wattlebridge principals** whether anything was actually agreed. Until then, treat every point as open.
- **The market claims are partly true.** Caps of 10–20%, baskets around 1% and 12–18 month periods are common for general warranties. But in that market, those limits usually come with standard carve-outs: fundamental warranties, tax, fraud and specific indemnities. Buyer-knowledge exclusions are not a settled market norm.
- **The Disclosure Letter contradicts the cover note.** The note downplays several matters ("addressed", "adequate", "not expected to be material", "ordinary course"). The Seller's own letter says each of them is unresolved (§§2–6, 8, 11). Rely on the letter, not the note.

---

## 1. How the liability package fits together (the most important point)

Three provisions combine to remove most of the Buyer's protection:

1. **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
2. **Buyer-knowledge exclusion** covering anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
3. **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 / 13).

Every material risk identified in due diligence (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006, Sandbar) is in the data room. So it would be both disclosed against and excluded by Buyer knowledge. Any remaining claim would then be capped, subject to the basket and time-barred. The practical result is near-zero recourse for the very risks we have found.

**Response:** reject each of the three provisions on its own terms (below). Also make sure every specific indemnity is expressly carved out of disclosure, Buyer knowledge and the general limitations.

---

## 2. Liability limitations

| Clause | Seller position | Issue | Buyer push-back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **12.1 Cap** | 20% (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims | Acceptable as a general cap **only if** it is limited to general warranties | Keep 20% (or seek more if W&I insurance is not used). Carve-outs: title/capacity and tax up to 100% of price; specific indemnities subject to a separate cap of at least 100% of price, or uncapped; fraud uncapped. |
| **12.2 Thresholds** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket, recover only the excess | A deductible basket costs the Buyer AUD 250k every time. The de minimis could also be gamed by splitting related claims. | Tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from dollar one). De minimis around AUD 10k, with claims from the same or related facts aggregated. Neither threshold applies to fundamental warranties, tax, indemnities or fraud. |
| **12.3 / 13 Time limits** | 18 months; any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | The default rule would silently catch indemnities, covenants, leakage, price adjustments and tax | 18 months for general warranties is acceptable. Tax: statutory amendment period plus 6 months (practically 5+ years). Title/capacity: 6–7 years. Indemnities: separate periods tied to the relevant risk. Reverse the default so limitations apply **only** where expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental / title** | Same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Not market. Title is the core of a share sale. A AUD 4.8m cap on a AUD 24m title failure is indefensible. | Reject outright. Cap at 100% of price, no thresholds, 6–7 years, and outside any Buyer-knowledge or disclosure qualification. |
| **9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance** | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Would protect fraud and wilful concealment, and attempts to limit misleading or deceptive conduct claims (ACL s 18 cannot be fully excluded, but non-reliance clauses can defeat the reliance element) | Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives. Exclusive remedy must not limit indemnities, covenants, leakage, specific performance or injunctive relief. Non-reliance must not cover the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter or fraud. |

---

## 3. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter)

- **1.1–1.2 general disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.** Reject. Disclosure should be limited to matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact. At most, accept deemed disclosure of an agreed, indexed data room copy, on the same "fair disclosure" standard and with no general disclosure of public records.
- **No disclosure against** title/capacity warranties, tax warranties (other than specific items) or any specific indemnity.
- **1.4 "no admission".** Acceptable as a non-admission statement, provided it cannot be read as preventing a disclosed matter from founding an indemnity claim.
- **Specific disclosures (§§2–10).** These are actually useful to us. The Seller has confirmed in writing that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, the Ironquay assignment and the DD-006 investigation are all **outstanding**, and that the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow. Use those admissions to support the protections below.

---

## 4. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

The clause covers the Buyer **or its advisers**, knowledge that is actual or constructive ("discoverable"), and the data room and public records. It is extremely broad.

**Push back:** the preferred position is a pro-sandbagging clause, under which no Buyer knowledge, investigation or due diligence affects any claim. The fallback is that only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter qualify the Warranties. If the Seller insists, limit it to the **actual** knowledge of a short list of named Buyer individuals, of specific facts known to amount to a breach, and never in respect of indemnities, title or tax.

---

## 5. Specific matters

### 5.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): about 30% of revenue

**Problem:** the Disclosure Letter (§2) says there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and would treat delivery of a consent letter as satisfying the condition, even if the consent is conditional.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **Condition Precedent**: an unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably). Any consent conditions that bind the Company or the Buyer after Completion must be approved by the Buyer.
- The condition is waivable **only by the Buyer**. Include a sunset date and a Buyer termination right.
- Strengthen the Seller obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with the Buyer consulted on communications with Bluefen.
- If the Buyer later agrees to waive, require a specific indemnity for loss of the contract, or a price adjustment or retention.

### 5.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): about AUD 3.2m

**Problem:** the deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release *after* Completion. The facility has a change-control clause (8.1), which may trigger default or acceleration at Completion. The security may extend to the Company's assets or even the shares.

**Push back:**
- Repay the facility **at Completion out of the price**. Require a payoff letter, a signed deed of release and PPSR financing-change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately) as **Completion deliverables**.
- Treat the full payoff amount, including break costs, interest and fees, as Debt deducted from the price in the funds flow.
- Include a title warranty that the shares are free of all Encumbrances. Check that Riverlark holds no share mortgage (see 5.10).
- Include an indemnity for any amounts arising under the facility.

### 5.3 DD-005 closing bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs

**Problem:** the Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller". However, they are liabilities of the **Company**, which the Buyer will own. They are not in the funds flow (DL §5), and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not addressed.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and **all associated on-costs** (PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation and similar) as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
- Include an uncapped indemnity for any shortfall or related employee claims.
- Confirm in the Accounts whether any amounts are accrued, to avoid a double deduction.

### 5.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Problem:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is recorded as open, there is no evidence of payment and there is no confirmatory assignment (DL §4). The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, not the IP risk. The Company may not own material code or IP.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion, the Seller procures payment of all SOW3 fees, cleared-funds evidence and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** (including moral rights consents) from Ironquay. Make these a CP or Completion deliverable.
- Expand the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have full rights in the SOW3 materials. That includes third-party claims, licence fees, re-engineering and replacement costs, and business interruption. The indemnity sits outside the cap, basket and Buyer-knowledge provisions.
- Verify independently (creditor ledger, bank statements, and an Ironquay confirmation if possible).

### 5.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Problem:** about 1,240 records containing personal information were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unresolved (DL §6). Calling it "not expected to be material" is unsupported.

**Timing:** under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete an assessment within 30 days. The matter was known by 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November. Ask immediately when the incident occurred, whether the assessment was completed, and whether the OAIC and affected individuals were notified. A missed statutory timeframe is a separate exposure. Penalties have been significantly increased under recent reforms.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenants:
  - complete an independent forensic investigation, with a report to the Buyer;
  - make the NDB assessment and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation;
  - make reasonable efforts to recover or secure deletion of the file;
  - notify affected customers if their contracts require it.
- A specific indemnity for all loss from the incident: regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, notification costs and third-party claims. It sits outside the cap, basket, de minimis and Buyer-knowledge exclusion and runs for at least 3–4 years.
- Specific privacy and data-security warranties, not qualified by DL §6.
- Consider a **retention or escrow** until regulatory exposure is resolved.
- Check whether cyber insurance responds and whether the incident triggers notice obligations in Bluefen or other key customer contracts.

### 5.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: AUD 330,000 aggregate

**Problem:** these are three "related" renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Seller asks to be "read together". Each sits below the AUD 250k basket and may be below the SPA's ordinary-course or consent thresholds, which suggests a split commitment. The Seller has not said whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL §8). It is also unclear whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 and the renewal terms. Confirm the counterparty relationship, term, termination rights and when the commitments were made.
- Make the conduct-of-business covenant apply to **aggregated** related commitments.
- If Sandbar is Seller-connected, treat the payments as **Leakage**, recoverable dollar for dollar.
- If the commitments were made outside the ordinary course or are not needed by the business, require pre-Completion termination at the Seller's cost, a price adjustment or a specific indemnity.

### 5.7 Tax and IP warranties

"Settled under the general regime" is not acceptable.
- **Tax:** a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (including tax arising from the bonuses and from Completion itself). Cap up to 100% of price, no thresholds, time limit of the statutory amendment period plus 6 months, Buyer conduct of tax claims, and no general disclosure.
- **IP:** full IP ownership and non-infringement warranties, and a specific indemnity for Ironquay (5.4). Consider treating core IP ownership as a quasi-fundamental warranty with an extended cap and period.

### 5.8 Office lease (DD-007)

The Seller describes a notification obligation only, not landlord consent (DL §7). **Review the lease ourselves.** Check change-of-control definitions, deemed-assignment clauses, any bank guarantee, and any parent guarantee that may need replacing. Seek a warranty that no consent is required, and a covenant to give notice on time.

### 5.9 Mossvale (DD-009)

The clause restricts assignment, and the Seller says it is not triggered by a share sale (DL §9). **Verify independently.** Many clauses deem a change of control to be an assignment. Seek a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right, other than those listed.

### 5.10 Title (DD-012)

**Problem:** title is evidenced only by the Company's own register. The Seller expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified it (DL §10).

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the register with ASIC records, the share certificates and the issue history.
- Check the PPSR for security over the shares (Riverlark in particular).
- Check the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption rights, options, convertible notes, ESOP or phantom equity. The employees receiving the DD-005 bonuses may hold such rights.
- Require pre-emption waivers and cancellation of any options at Completion.
- The title warranty is fundamental (see section 2).

---

## 6. Further structural protections to consider

- **Retention or escrow** from the price (for example AUD 1.5–2.5m), held for 12–24 months, to secure indemnities for DD-006, Ironquay, Sandbar and tax. The Seller is a venture vehicle and may distribute the proceeds, so credit risk is real.
- **Seller guarantor or creditworthiness covenant** if no escrow is agreed.
- **W&I insurance.** If the Seller wants low caps, a buy-side policy can fill the gap. Known matters are excluded under such policies, so the specific indemnities above remain essential either way.
- **MAC / termination right** between signing and Completion (Bluefen, DD-006 escalation).
- **Completion accounts or locked box.** Confirm the mechanics so that Debt includes Riverlark, the bonuses with on-costs, and Transaction Costs.

---

## 7. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommendation | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / not re-open" framing | Don't accept. Confirm with principals what, if anything, was agreed. | High |
| 2 | General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2) | Specific and fair disclosure only. No disclosure against title, tax or indemnities. | **Critical** |
| 3 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Delete (pro-sandbagging), or limit to actual knowledge of named individuals. Never against indemnities, title or tax. | **Critical** |
| 4 | Limitations apply to "all Claims" (9.3/12.8/13/20.5) | Reverse the default. Carve out fraud, indemnities, covenants, leakage and tax. | **Critical** |
| 5 | Title/capacity under general cap | Reject. Cap at 100% of price, 6–7 years, no thresholds. | **Critical** |
| 6 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay at Completion from the price, with a deed of release and PPSR discharges as deliverables. | **Critical** |
| 7 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Buyer-only waivable CP: unconditional consent with cl 11.3 satisfied, a stronger endeavours standard and a walk right. | **Critical** |
| 8 | DD-006 privacy incident | Urgent fact check on NDB timing. Investigation covenants, uncapped specific indemnity, retention. | **Critical** |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Payment and confirmatory assignment as a CP or deliverable. Full IP indemnity outside the limits. | High |
| 10 | Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs | Deduct from the price as Debt or Transaction Costs, with an indemnity. | High |
| 11 | Tax | Stand-alone tax indemnity, with a longer period and cap. | High |
| 12 | Basket / de minimis | Tipping basket, de minimis around AUD 10k, aggregation of related claims. | Medium |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Diligence the counterparty and terms. Treat as Leakage if related, otherwise terminate or indemnify. | Medium |
| 14 | General cap 20% | Acceptable for general warranties only, given the carve-outs above. | Medium |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Verify the clauses ourselves and obtain no-consent warranties. | Medium |
| 16 | Escrow / W&I / MAC | Seek a retention (or guarantor), consider W&I, include a MAC right. | High |

**Immediate actions:**
1. Confirm the principal-level position on "agreed" terms.
2. Obtain the DD-006 incident timeline and NDB assessment status.
3. Pull and review DD-003, DD-004, DD-007, DD-008, DD-009 and DD-011 directly.
4. Run ASIC and PPSR searches on the Company and its shares.
5. Request the Riverlark payoff letter and the Bluefen consent correspondence.
6. Prepare the SPA mark-up and a counter-Disclosure Letter on the basis above.

Any consent conditions that bind the Company or the Buyer after Completion must be approved by the Buyer.
- The condition is waivable **only by the Buyer**. Include a sunset date and a Buyer termination right.
- Strengthen the Seller obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with the Buyer consulted on communications with Bluefen.
- If the Buyer later agrees to waive, require a specific indemnity for loss of the contract, or a price adjustment or retention.

### 5.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): about AUD 3.2m

**Problem:** the deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release *after* Completion. The facility has a change-control clause (8.1), which may trigger default or acceleration at Completion. The security may extend to the Company's assets or even the shares.

**Push back:**
- Repay the facility **at Completion out of the price**. Require a payoff letter, a signed deed of release and PPSR financing-change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them immediately) as **Completion deliverables**.
- Treat the full payoff amount, including break costs, interest and fees, as Debt deducted from the price in the funds flow.
- Include a title warranty that the shares are free of all Encumbrances. Check that Riverlark holds no share mortgage (see 5.10).
- Include an indemnity for any amounts arising under the facility.

### 5.3 DD-005 closing bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs

**Problem:** the Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller". However, they are liabilities of the **Company**, which the Buyer will own. They are not in the funds flow (DL §5), and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not addressed.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and **all associated on-costs** (PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation and similar) as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the deduction.
- Include an uncapped indemnity for any shortfall or related employee claims.
- Confirm in the Accounts whether any amounts are accrued, to avoid a double deduction.

### 5.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Problem:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is recorded as open, there is no evidence of payment and there is no confirmatory assignment (DL §4). The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, not the IP risk. The Company may not own material code or IP.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion, the Seller procures payment of all SOW3 fees, cleared-funds evidence and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** (including moral rights consents) from Ironquay. Make these a CP or Completion deliverable.
- Expand the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have full rights in the SOW3 materials. That includes third-party claims, licence fees, re-engineering and replacement costs, and business interruption. The indemnity sits outside the cap, basket and Buyer-knowledge provisions.
- Verify independently (creditor ledger, bank statements, and an Ironquay confirmation if possible).

### 5.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Problem:** about 1,240 records containing personal information were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unresolved (DL §6). Calling it "not expected to be material" is unsupported.

**Timing:** under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete an assessment within 30 days. The matter was known by 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November. Ask immediately when the incident occurred, whether the assessment was completed, and whether the OAIC and affected individuals were notified. A missed statutory timeframe is a separate exposure. Penalties have been significantly increased under recent reforms.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenants:
  - complete an independent forensic investigation, with a report to the Buyer;
  - make the NDB assessment and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation;
  - make reasonable efforts to recover or secure deletion of the file;
  - notify affected customers if their contracts require it.
- A specific indemnity for all loss from the incident: regulatory penalties, investigation and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, notification costs and third-party claims. It sits outside the cap, basket, de minimis and Buyer-knowledge exclusion and runs for at least 3–4 years.
- Specific privacy and data-security warranties, not qualified by DL §6.
- Consider a **retention or escrow** until regulatory exposure is resolved.
- Check whether cyber insurance responds and whether the incident triggers notice obligations in Bluefen or other key customer contracts.

### 5.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: AUD 330,000 aggregate

**Problem:** these are three "related" renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Seller asks to be "read together". Each sits below the AUD 250k basket and may be below the SPA's ordinary-course or consent thresholds, which suggests a split commitment. The Seller has not said whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL §8). It is also unclear whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 and the renewal terms. Confirm the counterparty relationship, term, termination rights and when the commitments were made.
- Make the conduct-of-business covenant apply to **aggregated** related commitments.
- If Sandbar is Seller-connected, treat the payments as **Leakage**, recoverable dollar for dollar.
- If the commitments were made outside the ordinary course or are not needed by the business, require pre-Completion termination at the Seller's cost, a price adjustment or a specific indemnity.

### 5.7 Tax and IP warranties

"Settled under the general regime" is not acceptable.
- **Tax:** a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (including tax arising from the bonuses and from Completion itself). Cap up to 100% of price, no thresholds, time limit of the statutory amendment period plus 6 months, Buyer conduct of tax claims, and no general disclosure.
- **IP:** full IP ownership and non-infringement warranties, and a specific indemnity for Ironquay (5.4). Consider treating core IP ownership as a quasi-fundamental warranty with an extended cap and period.

### 5.8 Office lease (DD-007)

The Seller describes a notification obligation only, not landlord consent (DL §7). **Review the lease ourselves.** Check change-of-control definitions, deemed-assignment clauses, any bank guarantee, and any parent guarantee that may need replacing. Seek a warranty that no consent is required, and a covenant to give notice on time.

### 5.9 Mossvale (DD-009)

The clause restricts assignment, and the Seller says it is not triggered by a share sale (DL §9). **Verify independently.** Many clauses deem a change of control to be an assignment. Seek a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right, other than those listed.

### 5.10 Title (DD-012)

**Problem:** title is evidenced only by the Company's own register. The Seller expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified it (DL §10).

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the register with ASIC records, the share certificates and the issue history.
- Check the PPSR for security over the shares (Riverlark in particular).
- Check the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption rights, options, convertible notes, ESOP or phantom equity. The employees receiving the DD-005 bonuses may hold such rights.
- Require pre-emption waivers and cancellation of any options at Completion.
- The title warranty is fundamental (see section 2).

## 6. Further structural protections to consider

- **Retention or escrow** from the price (for example AUD 1.5–2.5m), held for 12–24 months, to secure indemnities for DD-006, Ironquay, Sandbar and tax. The Seller is a venture vehicle and may distribute the proceeds, so credit risk is real.
- **Seller guarantor or creditworthiness covenant** if no escrow is agreed.
- **W&I insurance.** If the Seller wants low caps, a buy-side policy can fill the gap. Known matters are excluded under such policies, so the specific indemnities above remain essential either way.
- **MAC / termination right** between signing and Completion (Bluefen, DD-006 escalation).
- **Completion accounts or locked box.** Confirm the mechanics so that Debt includes Riverlark, the bonuses with on-costs, and Transaction Costs.
